clue.text: Fascinated, but about to get hurt

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to be hurt is to be harmed

explanation.surface: Someone enchanted by a person or thing, yet on the brink of being wounded by it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be charmed is to be captivated or delighted, a straight synonym for fascinated.

clue.text: See children's fiction around — it's definitely not original

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced the same as see, a crossword convention

indicators.note: around says the word for fiction goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a stale children's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché is a phrase or idea worn out by overuse, the opposite of fresh or original.

clue.text: Victor embraced by lady I fancy with enthusiasm

indicators.note: embraced by says the letter goes inside the other letters
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Victor hugged by a woman the speaker is keen on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like 'desire'; it rearranges LADY I to AIDLY, and V goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidly means eagerly, keenly, an adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text: Cycling cape's under dog meat

indicators.note: under says, in this down clue, the cape comes below the dog

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: cycling means the letters move round, the first going to the end

parts.note: a poncho is a sleeveless cape-like garment

explanation.surface: A cyclist's cape draped beneath a dog's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves P from the front of PONCHO to the end, making ONCHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutton chop is a cut of sheep meat from the loin.

clue.text: Time inside does maybe discourage

indicators.note: inside says the letter for time goes within the other word

parts.note: does are female deer, so an example of deer

explanation.surface: Whether a spell in prison actually puts people off crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like the verb; it is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to put someone off doing something, to discourage them.

clue.text: One chapter ending writer's cutting

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: ending says take the final letter of chapter

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: A writer's prose described as sharp, with one chapter's conclusion singled out as savage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting remarks are sharp and sarcastic, which is exactly what acerbic describes.

clue.text: Upset at pianist for starters

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed with a piano player over the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian appetisers served before the main meal, so first courses.

clue.text: Flat number son mislaid

indicators.note: mislaid means lost, so the letter for son goes missing

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A boy has lost the number of the apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, as does 'number'; it means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means smooth and level, the same as flat.

clue.text: Streaked — checked name's hidden

indicators.note: hidden says the letter for name is tucked away inside the other word

parts.note: to bridle is to restrain or check, as with a horse

explanation.surface: Someone ran naked, and the name was checked and kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaked' looks like running naked; it means marked with streaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A brindled animal has a coat marked with darker streaks on a tawny or grey ground.

clue.text: Well-spoken German wearing sword

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the sword goes round the letter

parts.note: a cutlass is a short curved sword

explanation.surface: A refined German with a blade at his side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a precise, upper-class British way of speaking, so polished and well-spoken.

clue.text: Right away Vlad would demonstrate he's not very bright

parts.note: Vlad is the setter, so 'Vlad would' is I'D, the setter speaking

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is dropped from what precedes

parts.note: to riot is to protest violently in the streets

explanation.surface: The setter claims that, with right absent, he would protest to show someone is dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' looks like 'immediately'; here it tells you to remove R from I'D RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a fool, someone lacking intelligence, so the phrase describes the person.

clue.text: Completely thoughtless opening, with most of this hotel requiring refurbishment

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of thoughtless
a building needing refurbishment is to be done over, so these letters are rearranged
most of a word is all but its last letter, so this is cut short

explanation.surface: A careless start, and a hotel badly in need of renovation, all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring refurbishment' rearranges THI and HOTEL into OTHEHILT, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to the hilt means doing it fully, as a sword driven in up to its handle.

clue.text: Serf I engaged to secure plant

indicators.note: engaged means held inside, so I goes into the word for serf

parts.note: a helot was a serf in ancient Sparta
to rope something is to tie it fast, to secure it

explanation.surface: A peasant labourer hired to tie down a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden shrub with fragrant purple flowers that turn towards the sun.

clue.text: One's most admired feature of Hello? Diddly-squat on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
a feature of something is a part of it, so the letters sit inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A greeting met with nothing at all, which on reflection is someone's best quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'One's most admired feature' as the definition, leaving no word to signal the hiding; 'feature of' is that signal, so the definition is 'One's most admired'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person someone worships or looks up to above all others.

clue.text: Nothing up? Force Frenchman into possible trouble

indicators.note: up says, in this down clue, the letters are read upwards

parts.note: FA, short for sweet Fanny Adams, means nothing at all
a flic is French slang for a police officer, a man of the force

indicators.note: possible suggests one possible arrangement of the word into

explanation.surface: A worried question about forcing a Frenchman into likely trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FA into AF; 'possible' rearranges INTO to TION. 'Into' looks like a link word but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An affliction is a cause of suffering or distress, a trouble.

clue.text: Ads on other side where, hopefully, 18 25's provided

indicators.note: on says the scrambled side comes after the rest

parts.note: a school class is where pupils are supposed to absorb their lessons
provided means if, on condition that

indicators.note: other says the letters of side are made different, rearranged

explanation.surface: Advertisements printed overleaf from where the paper hopes its readers pick something up.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is the long answer, which describes what should happen in a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Classifieds are the small advertisements in a newspaper, grouped by category.

clue.text: Seat in bar maybe not his?

definitions.text: Seat in bar maybe not his?

indicators.note: maybe signals one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A bar stool is unlikely to be occupied by someone who never drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a seat in a bar is hardly the teetotaller's.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refuses alcohol, so would not be found occupying a seat in a pub bar.

clue.text: Palace turned over City and Gunners (exaggerating player B's input)

indicators.note: input says the actor and letter are put into the other pieces
turned over says, in this down clue, the city's letters are flipped

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a city
RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners
a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: Crystal Palace beaten by Manchester City and Arsenal, with one player overplaying his part.
explanation.walkthrough: City, Gunners (Arsenal) and Palace look like English football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress at Granada in Spain.

clue.text: Attacked after broadcast, alas, is duke out of the country?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread around
out of says the letters for the country are removed from duke

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is the country in question

explanation.surface: A duke, sadly abroad, is set upon following a radio talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' leaves DE; 'after broadcast' scrambles the rest with it. The question mark admits the duke is not really exiled.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, so assailed means attacked.

clue.text: Quietly going, sacked? Bland response … well, lies (1 down justifying why not)

definitions.text: Quietly going, sacked? Bland response … well, lies (1 down justifying why not)

indicators.note: a place that is sacked is plundered and turned upside down, so the letters are jumbled
going means leaving, so the letter for quietly disappears from the words

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A boss asked whether they will go quietly or be fired gives a stock reply, which is really untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from BLAND RESPONSE WELL LIES and rearrange what is left. The bracket says the stock phrase is a cliché, which is why nobody ends up sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock official reply after a failure, promising improvement while avoiding blame or resignation.

clue.text: After exam, one finally has a ball

indicators.note: after says, in this down clue, the rest follows the exam

parts.note: an exam is a test
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: finally says take the last letter of has

explanation.surface: A student celebrates the end of exams with a great party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a ball' looks like a dance; it is a testicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A testis is a testicle, slang for which is a ball.

clue.text: Like to hear about America's leader? Wrong

parts.note: as means like, in the way that

indicators.note: about says the word for hear goes round the letter

parts.note: a court tries a case when it hears it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone eager for news of the American president, who has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' looks like a sound clue; it is TRY, as a court hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone astray means off course or wrong, as a plan can go astray.

clue.text: Like name for boy

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of, like

explanation.surface: Asking for a name similar to one suitable for a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan is a common male first name, so it can stand for a boy.

clue.text: Causes of traffic hold-ups

parts.note: a hold-up is also an armed robbery, and those who seize vehicles at gunpoint commit such robberies on traffic

explanation.surface: What makes cars back up on the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold-ups' looks like delays; it is robberies, and the traffic is the stolen cars.
explanation.definitionFit: These criminals seize cars from their drivers by force, so they hold up traffic in the robbery sense.

clue.text: Law supported by one biblical region

indicators.note: supported by says, in this down clue, the letter sits below

parts.note: Jude Law is an English actor
A means one

explanation.surface: A legal code backed by one region of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law' looks like legal code; it is the actor Jude Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Judea was the southern part of ancient Palestine named in the Bible.

clue.text: Report in paper sent

indicators.note: report means a spoken account, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: something in paper is wrapped

explanation.surface: A report is put into a newspaper and dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' looks like dispatched; it means sent into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means enraptured, and to be sent is old slang for being thrilled.

clue.text: See 18
Bury's season hasn't started

indicators.note: a word that hasn't started has lost its first letter

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: The football club Bury has yet to kick off its campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a Lancashire town whose football club was expelled from the league in 2019, so 'Bury's season' looks like football; capitalised, 'Bury' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, a formal synonym for bury.

clue.text: One checking car's height

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
a tor is a rocky hill or high point

explanation.surface: A mechanic measuring how tall a vehicle stands.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines accounts, a person whose job is to inspect and verify.

clue.text: Lady guards breeding ground! Pardon?

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so the lady's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Amy is a woman's name, so a lady
a nest is where birds breed

explanation.surface: A woman protecting a nursery spot, and someone asking her to repeat herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon?' looks like a request to repeat; it is the noun meaning official forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general official pardon granted to offenders.
